definition: The C structure underlying all Python objects in CPython, containing reference count (ob_refcnt) and type pointer (ob_type).
simpleExplanation: Every value in Python (numbers, lists, functions) is wrapped inside a PyObject header in memory.
technicalExplanation: Defined in CPython header files, PyObject holds ob_refcnt (8 bytes) and *ob_type pointer (8 bytes), ensuring uniform memory management across dynamic types.

definition: The unique memory address of a Python object, returned by id(). Tested using the 'is' operator.
simpleExplanation: Identity tests whether two variables point to the exact same physical memory block.
technicalExplanation: In CPython, id(obj) returns the memory address pointer cast as an integer. 'a is b' evaluates to '((uintptr_t)a == (uintptr_t)b)'.

definition: CPython's primary memory management strategy where objects maintain a counter of active references.
simpleExplanation: Python counts how many variables point to an object. When the count drops to zero, the object is immediately deallocated.
technicalExplanation: Incremented on assignment or parameter passing (Py_INCREF) and decremented on scope exit or reassignment (Py_DECREF). When ob_refcnt == 0, tp_dealloc is invoked.

definition: CPython's secondary cycle-detecting garbage collector that identifies self-referential object cycles.
simpleExplanation: A background cleaner that destroys isolated islands of objects pointing to each other.
technicalExplanation: Operates on 3 generations (Gen 0, 1, 2) using trial-deletion algorithms to calculate effective reference counts (gc_refs).

definition: The property of an object allowing its internal state or payload to be modified in-place without changing its identity.
simpleExplanation: Mutable objects (lists, dicts) can be changed after creation. Immutable objects (ints, strings, tuples) cannot.
technicalExplanation: Immutable objects retain fixed payload memory. Modifications to immutable types instantiate new objects with different memory addresses.

definition: Platform-independent intermediate representation compiled from Python source files (.pyc), executed by the CPython virtual machine loop.
simpleExplanation: Low-level instructions created by Python compiler before running code line by line.
technicalExplanation: Bytecode opcodes (e.g. LOAD_FAST, BINARY_OP) are dispatched by PyEval_EvalFrameDefault loop in CPython C codebase.

definition: A mathematical technique allowing models to dynamically weigh the importance of different tokens in a sequence relative to a target token.
simpleExplanation: A way for a neural network to focus on specific context words when processing text.
technicalExplanation: Computes Softmax((Q @ K.T) / sqrt(d_k)) @ V to produce contextualized token representations.

definition: A dense numerical vector representation of high-dimensional semantic data in a continuous vector space.
simpleExplanation: Converting words or documents into lists of numbers where similar meanings are close together.
technicalExplanation: Maps discrete token IDs into R^d dense vector space where spatial distance (e.g., Cosine) correlates with semantic similarity.

definition: An architecture combining external document retrieval with an LLM generator to ground answers in authoritative facts.
simpleExplanation: Giving an AI an open textbook (retriever) to read before answering questions (generator).
technicalExplanation: Query -> Dense/Sparse Retrieval -> Top-K Passages -> Prompt Construction -> LLM Generation -> Verified Response.

definition: A multi-layer graph-based Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) search algorithm offering logarithmic search complexity.
simpleExplanation: A fast highway system for searching billions of vectors in milliseconds.
technicalExplanation: Organizes vectors into multi-layer skip graphs where top layers allow long-distance greedy hops and bottom layers pinpoint nearest neighbors.

definition: An inference optimization technique that stores Key and Value attention matrices for previous tokens to avoid recomputation during autoregressive decoding.
simpleExplanation: Saving past token calculations so the LLM doesn't redo work for every generated word.
technicalExplanation: Reduces decoding time complexity per token from O(N^2) to O(N) by caching past K and V tensor projections across transformer layers.
